questions.question: Outline Air Pollutants
questions.solution_html:
• Outline Air Pollutants
  • Major air pollutants consist of Particulate Matter (PM2.5/PM10), Sulfur Dioxide (SO2), and Nitrogen Oxides (NOx)
  • which are primarily released from vehicle exhausts and industrial factories. Carbon Monoxide (CO) and Ground
  • level Ozone (O3) are also critical pollutants that trigger respiratory issues and contribute to environmental haze.
questions.final_answer: level Ozone (O3) are also critical pollutants that trigger respiratory issues and contribute to environmental haze

questions.question: Classify bacterial waterborne diseases.
questions.solution_html:
• Classify bacterial waterborne diseases.
  • Bacterial waterborne diseases are typically classified by the type of pathogen and its clinical manifestation
  • Enteric Infections: Primarily affecting the digestive tract, such as Cholera (Vibrio cholerae) and Typhoid Fever
  • (Salmonella Typhi).
  • Bacillary Infections: Causes acute inflammation of the colon, most notably Bacillary Dysentery (Shigella species)
questions.final_answer: Bacillary Infections: Causes acute inflammation of the colon, most notably Bacillary Dysentery (Shigella species)

questions.question: Classify the immunization of food borne infections .
questions.solution_html:
• Classify the immunization of food borne infections.
  • Immunization against foodborne pathogens involves both active and passive strategies to prevent outbreaks
  • Vaccination: Targeted shots for specific high-risk pathogens like Hepatitis A and Typhoid Fever to build long-term
  • immunity.
  • Passive Immunity: Use of pre-formed antibodies (immunoglobulins) in post-exposure scenarios to provide
  • immediate, short-term protection.

questions.question: What is acid rain?
questions.solution_html:
• Acid rain refers to any form of precipitation with acidic components, typically resulting from the reaction of Sulfur
  • Dioxide (SO2) and Nitrogen Oxides (NOx) with water, oxygen, and other chemicals in the atmosphere. It results in a
  • pH level lower than the natural average of 5.6, causing damage to ecosystems and infrastructure.
questions.final_answer: pH level lower than the natural average of 5.6, causing damage to ecosystems and infrastructure

questions.question: Explain the types of food hygiene.
questions.solution_html:
• Food hygiene is categorized into four main pillars to ensure safety from farm to table:Personal Hygiene: Proper
  • handwashing and health standards for food handlers.
  • Environmental Hygiene: Maintaining clean facilities, equipment, and effective pest control.
  • Food Handling Hygiene: Safe storage (temperature control), preparation (preventing cross-contamination), and
  • thorough cooking.

questions.question: Discuss high temp water treatment
questions.solution_html:
• This process uses heat to eliminate pathogenic microorganisms, typically through two methods
  • Boiling: Heating water to 100°C for at least one minute to kill most bacteria, viruses, and protozoa.
  • Pasteurization: Heating water to a specific temperature (e.g., 72°C) for a set duration to reduce the microbial load
  • without boiling, often used in large-scale solar water disinfection.
questions.final_answer: Option (c) for a set duration to reduce the microbial load

questions.question: Explain enzymatic spoilage.
questions.solution_html:
• Enzymatic spoilage occurs when natural enzymes within food remain active after harvest or slaughter, breaking
  • down cellular structures. This leads to browning (like in sliced apples), softening of tissues, and the development of
  • off-flavors, even in the absence of microbial growth.
questions.final_answer: off-flavors, even in the absence of microbial growth

questions.question: Write about solid waste managment.
questions.solution_html:
• This is the systematic control of the generation, storage, collection, transport, processing, and disposal of solid
  • waste. It prioritizes the "3 Rs" (Reduce, Reuse, Recycle) and utilizes methods like composting, incineration, and
  • sanitary landfills to minimize environmental and health impacts.
questions.final_answer: sanitary landfills to minimize environmental and health impacts

questions.question: Describe staphylococcal food poisioning.
questions.solution_html:
• Caused by ingesting toxins produced by Staphylococcus aureus, this illness is characterized by a very rapid onset
  • (usually 30 minutes to 8 hours). It typically stems from improper handling of "ready-to-eat" foods, as the bacteria
  • can multiply and produce heat-stable toxins if food is left at room temperature.
questions.final_answer: can multiply and produce heat-stable toxins if food is left at room temperature

questions.question: Discuss the symptoms of bacillary dystentry.
questions.solution_html:
• Caused by Shigella bacteria, the primary symptoms include
  • Severe Mucoid Diarrhea: Frequent stools often containing blood and mucus.
  • Abdominal Cramping: Intense pain and "tenesmus" (a constant feeling of needing to pass stool).
  • Systemic Signs: High fever, nausea, and dehydration.
questions.final_answer: Systemic Signs: High fever, nausea, and dehydration

questions.question: Explain morphology of Hepatitis A Virus.
questions.solution_html:
• The Hepatitis A virus is a small, non-enveloped virus belonging to the Picornaviridae family. It features an
  • icosahedral capsid (roughly spherical) and contains a single-stranded RNA genome, making it highly resistant to
  • environmental stressors like heat and acid.
questions.final_answer: environmental stressors like heat and acid

questions.question: Examine the health risk of air pollution
questions.solution_html:
• Examine the health risk of air pollution
  • Air pollution impacts multiple body systems, leading to both acute and chronic conditions
  • Respiratory Issues: Aggravation of asthma, chronic bronchitis, and increased risk of lung cancer.
  • Cardiovascular Strain: Higher incidence of heart attacks and strokes due to systemic inflammation caused by fine
  • particulate matter entering the bloodstream.
  • Short Essay Questions

questions.question: Discuss indusrial waste disposal lead to water contamination
questions.solution_html:
• marks, Industrial waste concept – (2 marks)).
  • Industries often discharge untreated effluents containing heavy metals, toxic chemicals, and organic solvents
  • directly into water bodies. These pollutants alter the chemical composition of the water, making it toxic for aquatic
  • life and unsafe for human consumption. Seepage from industrial landfills can also leak into groundwater, leading to
  • long-term contamination of drinking water sources.
questions.final_answer: long-term contamination of drinking water sources

questions.question: Describe methods to detect egg spoilage.
questions.solution_html:
• The Float Test is a simple method where fresh eggs sink in water while spoiled eggs float due to increased air cells.
  • Candling involves holding the egg against a bright light to check for internal spots, blood rings, or a displaced yolk.
  • Sensory evaluation can detect spoilage through the presence of a "rotten egg" sulfur smell or a thin, watery
  • consistency of the whites.

questions.question: Investigate the causes of Waste Pollution.
questions.solution_html:
• Investigate the causes of Waste Pollution. / (Any four causes of waste pollution (1 mark) each)
  • Waste pollution is primarily caused by rapid urbanization and the over-consumption of non-biodegradable
  • materials like plastics and electronics. Inadequate waste collection systems and the lack of public awareness
  • regarding segregation lead to littering and illegal dumping. Industrial expansion and poor management of
  • hazardous materials further contribute to the accumulation of toxic waste in the environment
questions.final_answer: hazardous materials further contribute to the accumulation of toxic waste in the environment

questions.question: Classify hospital waste.
questions.solution_html:
• Classify hospital waste. / (Any 4 categories with examples – (4 marks))
  • Hospital waste is classified into Infectious Waste (swabs, bandages, cultures) and Pathological Waste (body parts
  • blood, fluids). It also includes Sharps (needles, scalpels), Pharmaceutical Waste (expired medicines), and General
  • Waste (paper, food packaging). Radioactive waste and chemical waste from labs are also categorized separately due
  • to their specific disposal requirements.

questions.question: State UV light.
questions.solution_html:
• Ultraviolet (UV) light is a form of electromagnetic radiation that acts as a powerful germicidal agent by damaging
  • the DNA of microorganisms. When pathogens are exposed to UV-C rays, they lose their ability to reproduce and
  • cause infections. It is widely used for sterilizing laboratory surfaces, treating drinking water, and purifying air in
  • medical facilities.

questions.question: Distinguish between influenze and tuberculosis.
questions.solution_html:
• on Tuberculosis – (2 marks))
  • Influenza is a viral respiratory infection characterized by sudden onset, high fever, and body aches, usually lasting
  • for a week. Tuberculosis is a chronic bacterial infection caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis that primarily affects
  • the lungs over a long period. While the flu is prevented by seasonal vaccines, TB requires a long-term course of
  • specialized antibiotics and has a much slower progression.
questions.final_answer: specialized antibiotics and has a much slower progression

questions.question: Illustrate factors affecting microbial growth.
questions.solution_html:
• Temperature, pH, Oxygen, Nutrient availability, Moisture – (4 marks))
  • Microbial growth is heavily influenced by Temperature, where most pathogens thrive between 5°Cand 60°C (the
  • danger zone). Moisture levels, or water activity, are essential for metabolic processes and cellular reproduction in
  • bacteria and fungi. The pH Level of the environment dictates growth, as most bacteria prefer neutral conditions
  • while molds can tolerate acidity. Lastly, the availability of Nutrients like carbon and nitrogen provides the energy
  • necessary for microbes to multiply

• This process uses heat to eliminate pathogenic microorganisms, typically through two methods
  • Boiling: Heating water to 100°C for at least one minute to kill most bacteria, viruses, and protozoa.
  • Pasteurization: Heating water to a specific temperature (e.g., 72°C) for a set duration to reduce the microbial load
  • without boiling, often used in large-scale solar water disinfection.
questions.final_answer: Option (c) for a set duration to reduce the microbial load

questions.question: Explain enzymatic spoilage.
questions.solution_html:
• Enzymatic spoilage occurs when natural enzymes within food remain active after harvest or slaughter, breaking
  • down cellular structures. This leads to browning (like in sliced apples), softening of tissues, and the development of
  • off-flavors, even in the absence of microbial growth.
questions.final_answer: off-flavors, even in the absence of microbial growth

questions.question: Write about solid waste managment.
questions.solution_html:
• This is the systematic control of the generation, storage, collection, transport, processing, and disposal of solid
  • waste. It prioritizes the "3 Rs" (Reduce, Reuse, Recycle) and utilizes methods like composting, incineration, and
  • sanitary landfills to minimize environmental and health impacts.
questions.final_answer: sanitary landfills to minimize environmental and health impacts

questions.question: Describe staphylococcal food poisioning.
questions.solution_html:
• Caused by ingesting toxins produced by Staphylococcus aureus, this illness is characterized by a very rapid onset
  • (usually 30 minutes to 8 hours). It typically stems from improper handling of "ready-to-eat" foods, as the bacteria
  • can multiply and produce heat-stable toxins if food is left at room temperature.
questions.final_answer: can multiply and produce heat-stable toxins if food is left at room temperature

questions.question: Discuss the symptoms of bacillary dystentry.
questions.solution_html:
• Caused by Shigella bacteria, the primary symptoms include
  • Severe Mucoid Diarrhea: Frequent stools often containing blood and mucus.
  • Abdominal Cramping: Intense pain and "tenesmus" (a constant feeling of needing to pass stool).
  • Systemic Signs: High fever, nausea, and dehydration.
questions.final_answer: Systemic Signs: High fever, nausea, and dehydration

questions.question: Explain morphology of Hepatitis A Virus.
questions.solution_html:
• The Hepatitis A virus is a small, non-enveloped virus belonging to the Picornaviridae family. It features an
  • icosahedral capsid (roughly spherical) and contains a single-stranded RNA genome, making it highly resistant to
  • environmental stressors like heat and acid.
questions.final_answer: environmental stressors like heat and acid

questions.question: Examine the health risk of air pollution
questions.solution_html:
• Examine the health risk of air pollution
  • Air pollution impacts multiple body systems, leading to both acute and chronic conditions
  • Respiratory Issues: Aggravation of asthma, chronic bronchitis, and increased risk of lung cancer.
  • Cardiovascular Strain: Higher incidence of heart attacks and strokes due to systemic inflammation caused by fine
  • particulate matter entering the bloodstream.

questions.question: Discuss indusrial waste disposal lead to water contamination
questions.solution_html:
• marks, Industrial waste concept – (2 marks)).
  • Industries often discharge untreated effluents containing heavy metals, toxic chemicals, and organic solvents
  • directly into water bodies. These pollutants alter the chemical composition of the water, making it toxic for aquatic
  • life and unsafe for human consumption. Seepage from industrial landfills can also leak into groundwater, leading to
  • long-term contamination of drinking water sources.
questions.final_answer: long-term contamination of drinking water sources

questions.question: Describe methods to detect egg spoilage.
questions.solution_html:
• The Float Test is a simple method where fresh eggs sink in water while spoiled eggs float due to increased air cells.
  • Candling involves holding the egg against a bright light to check for internal spots, blood rings, or a displaced yolk.
  • Sensory evaluation can detect spoilage through the presence of a "rotten egg" sulfur smell or a thin, watery
  • consistency of the whites.

questions.question: Investigate the causes of Waste Pollution.
questions.solution_html:
• Investigate the causes of Waste Pollution. / (Any four causes of waste pollution (1 mark) each)
  • Waste pollution is primarily caused by rapid urbanization and the over-consumption of non-biodegradable
  • materials like plastics and electronics. Inadequate waste collection systems and the lack of public awareness
  • regarding segregation lead to littering and illegal dumping. Industrial expansion and poor management of
  • hazardous materials further contribute to the accumulation of toxic waste in the environment
questions.final_answer: hazardous materials further contribute to the accumulation of toxic waste in the environment

questions.question: Classify hospital waste.
questions.solution_html:
• Classify hospital waste. / (Any 4 categories with examples – (4 marks))
  • Hospital waste is classified into Infectious Waste (swabs, bandages, cultures) and Pathological Waste (body parts
  • blood, fluids). It also includes Sharps (needles, scalpels), Pharmaceutical Waste (expired medicines), and General
  • Waste (paper, food packaging). Radioactive waste and chemical waste from labs are also categorized separately due
  • to their specific disposal requirements.

questions.question: State UV light.
questions.solution_html:
• Ultraviolet (UV) light is a form of electromagnetic radiation that acts as a powerful germicidal agent by damaging
  • the DNA of microorganisms. When pathogens are exposed to UV-C rays, they lose their ability to reproduce and
  • cause infections. It is widely used for sterilizing laboratory surfaces, treating drinking water, and purifying air in
  • medical facilities.

questions.question: Distinguish between influenze and tuberculosis.
questions.solution_html:
• on Tuberculosis – (2 marks))
  • Influenza is a viral respiratory infection characterized by sudden onset, high fever, and body aches, usually lasting
  • for a week. Tuberculosis is a chronic bacterial infection caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis that primarily affects
  • the lungs over a long period. While the flu is prevented by seasonal vaccines, TB requires a long-term course of
  • specialized antibiotics and has a much slower progression.
questions.final_answer: specialized antibiotics and has a much slower progression

questions.question: Illustrate factors affecting microbial growth.
questions.solution_html:
• Temperature, pH, Oxygen, Nutrient availability, Moisture – (4 marks))
  • Microbial growth is heavily influenced by Temperature, where most pathogens thrive between 5°Cand 60°C (the
  • danger zone). Moisture levels, or water activity, are essential for metabolic processes and cellular reproduction in
  • bacteria and fungi. The pH Level of the environment dictates growth, as most bacteria prefer neutral conditions
  • while molds can tolerate acidity. Lastly, the availability of Nutrients like carbon and nitrogen provides the energy
  • necessary for microbes to multiply
